subject.title: feat: retain iMessage tombstones and revisions

question: Should existing imsgcrawl archives change from replacement-based sync behavior to merge-by-default retention, with `sync --restore` required for destructive replacement?
rationale: This changes the observable behavior and upgrade expectations of the repository’s first archive release line; code review cannot determine whether maintainers want retention safety to supersede the prior replacement expectation.

options.title: Adopt merge by default
options.body: Accept the retention-first archive contract, keep `sync --restore` as the explicit destructive path, and require redacted upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve replacement default
options.body: Keep replacement behavior as the default and offer merge only through an explicit opt-in if compatibility with current users outweighs retention safety.

options.title: Split the contract change
options.body: Land independently reviewable tombstone and revision storage work later, after the default sync semantics are separately decided.

recommendation.title: Adopt merge by default
recommendation.body: Accept the retention-first archive contract, keep `sync --restore` as the explicit destructive path, and require redacted upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository policy identifies Josh as the decision point for archive-structure exceptions and this is an archive contract decision.
